name: Live-rig e2e after a team.rego/projection change: restart OPA + rebuild the usermgmt image + recreate the pod, then grep the e2e for OLD-contract cells
description: Running the e2e after a 6.7-style control-plane change needs THREE rig steps, in order: (1) restart OPA (docker restart opa-abac-opa) so it reloads the edited team.rego + permission_categories.json from the ./opa/policies mount (--watch unreliable) — verify with curl localhost:28181/v1/data/permission_categories + opa eval probes; (2) rebuild the usermgmt image with the NEW Java (docker build -q -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile . — a full Gradle-in-container build, slow); (3) recreate the pod: docker compose -p opa-abac-example -f infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml up -d --force-recreate usermgmt, then wait for localhost:28090/actuator/health. The CATALOG image does NOT need rebuilding (no catalog code changed; catalog cells decide via the shared OPA). Intended-break sweep: the existing e2e matrices encode the OLD contract — team-abac cell 8 ('viewer GET /members -> 403') and the permission-categories cells assert pre-6.7 outcomes; the list-members loosening flips viewer/member GET /members to 200, so REWRITE those cells (viewer lists 200 / mutates 403) and ADD explicit loosening cells. Add new cells via a Python json edit reusing the runner's existing --env-var tokens (senior_token/ladder_token/team_id/target1_uid). Result: permission-categories 31/31, team 12/12, all other matrices unaffected (list-members inert on catalog) -> 129 assertions across 10 matrices, 0 failed.

name: Trace the APISIX->OPA->app->DB chain into Jaeger locally
description: Phase B of the example rig adds end-to-end distributed tracing. Pattern that worked: (1) Jaeger v2 + embedded Badger (jaegertracing/jaeger:2.17.0, --config=jaeger-config.yaml) for persistent traces with no JVM (avoids aarch64 SIGILL of ES/OpenSearch). (2) APISIX opentelemetry plugin via plugin_attr.opentelemetry.collector.address=jaeger:4318, enabled per-route with {"opentelemetry":{"sampler":{"name":"always_on"}}}. (3) OTEL Java agent BAKED INTO the app image (ADD opentelemetry-javaagent.jar /opt/otel/agent.jar) and attached per-pod via -javaagent + OTEL_SERVICE_NAME/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://opa-abac-jaeger:4318/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf. (4) OPA with distributed_tracing.type=grpc,address=jaeger:4317 emits its own decision spans. Verified: GET /api/services returns [apisix, catalog-management-service, opa, jaeger]; one APISIX trace nests gateway->app->JPA/DB spans. Note: APISIX opa plugin does NOT propagate trace context into the OPA call, so OPA spans are a separate service, not nested — expected. All host ports for Jaeger(16686/4317/4318)/OPA(8181) clash with a running portal podman-machine, so remap host side to 2xxxx; in-network DNS (opa-abac-jaeger:4318, opa:8181) is unaffected.

Two docker-rig operational gotchas surfaced during the 2026-07-12 rig rebuild. (1) HOST-PORT / RUNTIME COLLISION: the machine runs the starter rig on DOCKER and a separate unrelated project (IdP/portal) on PODMAN simultaneously. The podman stack binds the CANONICAL ports (opa-standalone :8181, keycloak-abac :8888, apisix :9080, portal-postgres :5432) while the docker starter rig is remapped to +20000-style host ports (opa-abac-opa :28181, opa-abac-keycloak :28888, apisix :9085->9080). Any localhost probe of the starter OPA MUST use :28181, NOT :8181 — hitting :8181 lands on the podman OPA (a paas/projects bundle) and every data.catalog.* returns undefined. This caused a false 'wrong bundle mounted' finding in the 7.4 security review. Verify which OPA you are talking to with: curl -s localhost:28181/v1/policies | grep catalog. (2) deploy.sh build EXIT-CODE MASKING: a docker build that FAILS (e.g. the ADD https://github.com/.../opentelemetry-javaagent.jar step dying with 'unexpected EOF' under a flaky network) still let ./deploy.sh build report exit 0 in one observed run — the wrapper did not propagate the buildkit failure. Always check the tail of the build output for 'ERROR: failed to build' / 'RC=1', do not trust the deploy.sh exit code alone. Separately, docker's ADD <github-release-url> is itself flaky (redirect-to-CDN cache-key fetch); DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 did not help when Docker Hub base-layer pulls were ALSO failing (transient registry outage). When images are unchanged vs the tree, skip the rebuild entirely and deploy.sh up on the existing :local images.
resolution: RIG PROBE PORTS (docker starter, when podman IdP stack co-runs): OPA localhost:28181, Keycloak localhost:28888, gateway localhost:9085. In-network token mint still uses the compose network (docker run --network opa-abac-example_default -> keycloak:8888 INSIDE the docker net — that 8888 is the container port, unaffected by the host remap). Base infra ordering: ./deploy.sh down tears down base Postgres too, so a subsequent ./deploy.sh up errors 'Postgres not running' — run ./profile.sh up FIRST, then ./deploy.sh up --pods N. Rebuild only when app SOURCE changed since the :local image timestamp (git log --since=<image age> -- example-*/src); the catalog.rego / OPA policies are bind-mounted from disk (NOT baked into the app image), so a policy fix needs only an OPA container restart / rig up, never an app image rebuild.

description: ENABLE_OPA=0 is NOT a pure pod-env flip: deploy.sh passes ENABLE_OPA through to infra/apisix/init-routes.sh, which then OMITS the gateway's coarse allow-all opa plugin from the catalog-all route — so a naive two-pass guarded/baseline comparison conflates the gateway OPA hop with the app-side library gate. Also, opa.abac.enabled=false removes the starter's ENTIRE auto-config (class-level @ConditionalOnProperty), and until PR #61 the example apps had never booted that way (empty FilterRegistrationBean crashes Tomcat even disabled — getDescription() asserts; no AbacFilter = 401 wall on authenticated(); 4 components hard-injected starter beans).
resolution: For an identical-gateway baseline: after the ENABLE_OPA=0 deploy, re-run init-routes.sh with ENABLE_OPA=1 (the OPA container keeps running — deploy.sh up never stops it), and ASSERT the route posture per pass via the APISIX admin API (openid-connect + opa present on catalog-all). App-side: PR #61 gives the examples an honest unguarded profile (property-gated filter registration, gateway-trust chain, lazy starter-bean injection with fail-closed floors, UnguardedBootIT on real Tomcat). Lesson for planning: an ADR that pins a rig mechanism must include a 5-minute boot spike of that mechanism.

name: APISIX gateway plugin ordering for auth chain (oidc->enrich->opa)
description: On an APISIX route that does OIDC + identity enrichment + OPA, plugin execution order matters and is controlled by _meta.priority (HIGHER runs first), not by JSON key order. Proven chain (matches portal): openid-connect(2599) -> serverless-pre-function enricher(2500) -> opa(2000) = authenticate, then inject identity headers from the validated JWT, then authorize. WITHOUT an explicit override, serverless-pre-function defaults to a very high priority and would run BEFORE openid-connect (no validated token yet) — so you MUST pin its _meta.priority below openid-connect. The enricher is a small Lua that base64url-decodes the JWT payload (already verified by openid-connect; it only READS claims) and sets X-User-Id (sub) / X-Username (preferred_username) via core.request.set_header. Build the Lua-in-JSON via a Python helper (json.dumps) to avoid bash escaping bugs. Keycloak omits 'sub' from the access token unless you add an oidc-sub-mapper protocolMapper to the client in the realm export (access.token.claim=true).

content: The example rig (Docker) is designed to run SIMULTANEOUSLY with the maintainer's proprietary portal stack (podman-machine) — do NOT stop podman. They coexist because the rig deliberately publishes every host port in a SHIFTED range so nothing collides with the podman portal: gateway 9085 (not 9080), catalog pods 28081/28082 (BASE_PORT 28080, not the portal 18080 range), OPA 28181 (not 8181), Keycloak 28888 (not 8888), Jaeger 26686/24317/24318, Postgres 5433 (not 5432); APISIX admin 9180. In-network DNS (opa:8181, keycloak:8888, opa-abac-jaeger:4318) is unaffected by the host remap. Both engines coexist as separate VMs/daemons; the ONLY shared constraint is host ports (resolved by the shift) and machine RAM/CPU (lever is --pods, not engine interference). OPERATIONAL ORDERING GOTCHA: deploy.sh does NOT start the base Postgres — it asserts 'opa-abac-postgres' already exists and ERRORS with 'Postgres not running. Start base infra first: ./profile.sh up' otherwise. So the correct bring-up is: (1) ./profile.sh up (base Postgres on 5433, healthy), then (2) [ENABLE_OIDC=1] ./deploy.sh up --pods N (Jaeger/OPA/Keycloak/APISIX/etcd + N catalog pods; OIDC is OFF by default — set ENABLE_OIDC=1 to exercise Keycloak token minting + gateway auth; OPA + tracing are on by default). Expected-correct signals: GET :9085/actuator/health returns 302 (APISIX openid-connect redirecting to Keycloak — that's auth working, NOT a failure) — verify the app itself via a direct pod hit :28081/actuator/health => {status:UP}. The 'Found orphan containers [opa-abac-postgres]' compose warnings are harmless (Postgres belongs to the profile.sh project, the rest to the deploy.sh project).

description: Phase 5.9 e2e: the tag and team newman matrices failed on user-service endpoints (a define-tag 201 had no Location; a gated 403 returned application/json not application/problem+json) even after running ./deploy.sh build and redeploying. Root cause: ./deploy.sh build rebuilds ONLY the catalog app image (build_image). The user-management image (opa-abac-usermgmt:local) is rebuilt ONLY by build_usermgmt_image, which deploy.sh invokes lazily as 'usermgmt_image_exists || build_usermgmt_image' inside the up path — so when a stale usermgmt image already exists, NEITHER deploy.sh build NOR deploy.sh up rebuilds it. The pod therefore kept serving 6-day-old code (the legacy ApiError body, no Location). Catalog-side assertions passed because the catalog image WAS rebuilt; only the user-service-routed requests failed.
resolution: When a slice changes user-service code, force its image explicitly: docker build -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile . (build context is the repo ROOT for the multi-module Gradle build), then recreate the container: docker compose -p opa-abac-example -f infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml up -d --force-recreate, and wait for http://localhost:28090/actuator/health UP. Symptom signature: in a two-service e2e, contract assertions pass on catalog routes but fail on user-service routes with the OLD body shape -> suspect a stale usermgmt image, not a code bug. (Consider teaching deploy.sh build to also rebuild usermgmt when ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1.)

description: Local APISIX container-pool rig (deploy.sh) failed to start in several non-obvious ways: (1) APISIX 3.x reads etcd config under deployment.etcd, not a top-level 'etcd:' key — a top-level key is silently ignored, APISIX falls back to 127.0.0.1:2379, logs 'all etcd nodes are unavailable', and the container exits. (2) bitnami/etcd images are gone (Bitnami sunset their free Docker Hub catalog) -> 'manifest unknown'. (3) Host port clashes with a running portal podman-machine gvproxy: :9080 and the 18081/18082 range are already bound. (4) Killing Postgres mid-session (e.g. compose down --remove-orphans on one of the shared-project compose files) makes pods return 503 with java.net.UnknownHostException: opa-abac-postgres.
resolution: (1) Put etcd under deployment.etcd in apisix/config.yaml. (2) Use quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.x with explicit --listen-client-urls/--advertise-client-urls. (3) Use proxy port 9085 and pod base port 28080 (pods 28081+) to dodge the podman-machine. (4) All three composes share name: opa-abac-example so they share opa-abac-example_default; never run 'compose down --remove-orphans' on a single file — it deletes the others' containers. Pods auto-recover (HikariCP reconnect) within seconds once Postgres is back. Bonus: enable response-rewrite plugin and set X-Upstream-Addr=$upstream_addr on the route to prove round-robin.

description: SYMPTOM: 'ENABLE_SPA=1 ./deploy.sh up' aborts at require_postgres ('Postgres not running') even though ./profile.sh up already ran. ROOT CAUSE: profile.sh up ran while podman was the active runtime, so opa-abac-postgres landed on the podman machine (gvproxy holds host :5433); after switching to Docker Desktop, deploy.sh's 'docker ps | grep opa-abac-postgres' queries Docker Desktop and can't see the podman-side container. Compounding: the image build (plain 'docker build', no --builder) auto-selected the 'podman' buildx docker-container builder (log line: buildx_buildkit_podman), which would NOT load the image into Docker Desktop's store, so even a 'successful' build leaves docker compose unable to find opa-abac-catalog:local.
resolution: Pick ONE daemon and converge everything on it. (1) podman rm -f opa-abac-postgres to free :5433 from gvproxy; (2) docker buildx use desktop-linux (native docker driver -> loads images into the daemon store; the docker-container drivers do not without --load); (3) restart base infra on Docker Desktop (default context IS desktop-linux -> leave DOCKER_HOST unset); (4) re-run deploy.sh up. PREVENT: keep one runtime live; if switching runtimes mid-session, tear down the stranded stack first (host ports are held by gvproxy until the podman container is removed). Verified after: scripts/postman/run-spa-auth-smoke.sh -> 4/4 (no-token 401, invalid 401, valid 200 health + 200 read /api/v1/catalogs).

description: Keycloak realm-export import died at container start with 'Value too long for column DESCRIPTION CHARACTER VARYING(255)' — a client 'description' field in realm-export.json over 255 chars aborts the ENTIRE realm import (dev-mode H2 and real DBs share the column size), so Keycloak starts with NO realm and every dependent service 401s. The compose healthcheck (TCP on 8888) does NOT catch it — the port never opens, but the failure mode reads as 'keycloak slow to start'.
resolution: Keep realm-export.json description fields under 255 chars (move rationale to a JSON-adjacent doc or the ADR); after editing the export, docker compose up -d --force-recreate keycloak (dev-mode, no volume -> re-import) and grep the logs for 'Import finished successfully' before trusting the rig.

description: Wiring APISIX openid-connect to a Keycloak container hit two non-obvious failures: (1) 'unknown plugin [openid-connect]' on the route PUT — APISIX only loads plugins listed in config.yaml's top-level 'plugins:'; adding openid-connect there requires RECREATING the apisix container (editing the file isn't enough, and curl -sf swallows the 400 so the route silently lacks the plugin). (2) Keycloak issuer mismatch: Keycloak is hostname-aware, so the discovery doc + token issuer differ by how it's reached — in-network http://keycloak:8888 vs host http://localhost:28888. APISIX discovers + validates IN-NETWORK (issuer keycloak:8888), so a token minted against localhost:28888 has a mismatched issuer and is rejected. Tokens must be minted in-network or via the browser redirect flow.
resolution: (1) After changing config.yaml plugins, force-recreate apisix (docker compose up -d --force-recreate apisix) before seeding routes; don't trust curl -sf (drop -f or inspect the body). (2) Pin KC_HOSTNAME_URL=http://keycloak:8888 + KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false so the in-network issuer is stable; for testing, mint tokens in-network via 'docker run --network opa-abac-example_default curlimages/curl ... http://keycloak:8888/realms/catalog-demo/protocol/openid-connect/token'. Verified: no-token->302, valid in-network token->200, bad->401. ENABLE_OIDC gate keeps it opt-in. Service does NO JWT check (gateway-only auth, Phase 2).

description: Testcontainers ITs failed with 'Could not find a valid Docker environment' even though podman machine reported running. Root cause: the podman machine claimed State=running but its API socket file (ConnectionInfo.PodmanSocket.Path under TMPDIR) was MISSING (stale machine state), so the build's resolveDockerHost() (which checks file(path).exists()) returned null and Testcontainers fell back to default strategies that probe /var/run/docker.sock (a dead symlink to the absent podman sock) and the Docker Desktop CLI socket (not a usable API socket) — both fail. Exporting DOCKER_HOST in the shell does NOT help because the Gradle test worker fork does not inherit it and the build only injects DOCKER_HOST when resolveDockerHost() is non-null. ~/.testcontainers.properties docker.host was also not honored by the failing strategy order.
resolution: Restart the podman machine: podman machine stop then podman machine start. This recreates the API socket (start prints 'API forwarding listening on: /var/run/docker.sock'). Then resolveDockerHost() finds the socket via podman machine inspect and the build auto-injects DOCKER_HOST into the test task as designed. Environment fix, no code change. If podman is genuinely unavailable, point DOCKER_HOST at the Docker Desktop RAW socket (~/.docker/run/docker.sock, NOT the docker-cli.sock) so the build's priority-1 env branch fires.

title: Gateway-side identity/enrichment is demo scaffold; the library does real extraction
rationale: The example rig's gateway does OIDC termination (APISIX openid-connect) and a Lua serverless-pre-function that decodes the JWT and injects X-User-Id/X-Username for OPA. This gateway-side identity handling is DELIBERATELY a throwaway demo so the topology is visible/traceable end-to-end NOW, before the library exists. It is NOT the target architecture. The project thesis (POC-ROADMAP) is to be Spring-NATIVE with no gateway 'mediator': real subject/attribute extraction belongs in the library — opa-abac-spring-security's pluggable Authentication->AbacContext extractor (see mx-ea7974), feeding OpaAuthorizationManager / @OpaPreAuthorize, with the service doing its own fine-grained ABAC (two-layer model mx-7130a1). So in Phase 3 the demo Lua enricher gets removed; the app validates the JWT and extracts AbacContext itself. Keep the gateway doing only coarse auth (authn + a coarse OPA route check); push fine-grained, attribute-level decisions into the app via the library. Don't let the demo enricher calcify into the design.

description: Liquibase sql changesets that use Postgres jsonb operators containing '?' (jsonb_exists ?, ?| , ?&) fail at migration time with 'syntax error at or near $1' - the JDBC driver rewrites every ? as a bind-parameter placeholder before Postgres sees it. Surfaced in the 6.5 seed-sweep changeset (0006-permission-categories.yaml) where 'e.value ? ''read''' broke every Testcontainers IT boot.
resolution: Use the function forms instead of the operators in any SQL that flows through JDBC/Liquibase: jsonb_exists(col, 'key') for ?, jsonb_exists_any for ?|, jsonb_exists_all for ?&. Same semantics, no placeholder collision.

name: Adding a gateway-fronted service to the rig: the four steps, and the one everyone forgets
description:
ENABLE_MCP=1 (AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ T6) followed the ENABLE_SPA/ENABLE_DIRECTORY precedent: (1) infra/compose.<svc>.yaml on the shared opa-abac-example network + a Dockerfile; (2) deploy.sh — the flag force-enabling its prerequisites, <svc>_compose()/build_<svc>_image()/wait_<svc>_healthy(), up + down + status line; (3) pass the flag through to init-routes.sh; (4) THE FORGOTTEN ONE — infra/apisix/init-routes.sh needs an upstream + route. The catalog-all route is uri:/* at the APISIX DEFAULT priority 0, so it silently swallows any new path: without a route, POST /mcp is proxied to the catalog pool and 404s there, which reads as 'the new service is broken'. Priority ladder in use: catalog-all 0 < keycloak-proxy 50 < usermgmt 60 < mcp 65 < internal-blocked 70. Plugin set for an app that authorizes ITSELF = the usermgmt set (openid-connect + response-rewrite + tracing/cors), explicitly NOT the catalog An open source project to policy-enable your service.

Usage:
  opa [command]

Available Commands:
  bench        Benchmark a Rego query
  build        Build an OPA bundle
  capabilities Print the capabilities of OPA
  check        Check Rego source files
  completion   Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  deps         Analyze Rego query dependencies
  eval         Evaluate a Rego query
  exec         Execute against input files
  fmt          Format Rego source files
  help         Help about any command
  inspect      Inspect OPA bundle(s)
  parse        Parse Rego source file
  run          Start OPA in interactive or server mode
  sign         Generate an OPA bundle signature
  test         Execute Rego test cases
  version      Print the version of OPA

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for opa

Use "opa [command] --help" for more information about a command. gateway plugin. Also: every outbound base-URL must be overridden in-network — the shipped defaults are localhost, which in a pod is the pod; the ROLE-SOURCE url is the trap, since a wrong value denies every call with a policy-shaped error code. Keycloak protocol mappers that must yield a JSON array need jsonType.label=JSON with claim.value='["x"]'; jsonType.label=String mints a bare string, and a fail-closed extractor will correctly but confusingly deny it.
